What you're racing for

It's not the car. It's the lap.

MOS Racing is built around one honest loop: go out, find the limit, beat your own time — then someone else's.

Ghost leaderboard

Race the people ahead of you

Every clean lap uploads a ghost — a perfect recording of the run. Tap any time on the global board and that driver's ghost lines up beside you, corner for corner, so you can see exactly where the tenths are hiding.

The Eifelring GP

One circuit. A lifetime of tenths.

A laser-scanned grand-prix layout with real elevation, cambered kerbs, and a run-off that punishes greed. Cut a corner or drop wheels off the tarmac and the lap goes invalid — no shortcuts to the top.

Feel & sound

You'll hear the grip go before you feel it

Engine note is generated live from the drivetrain — no loops, real revs. Haptics speak the surface, not the steering: a hard buzz over the kerbs, a rough stutter the instant the tires start to slide.

The grid

Three cars, three ways to be fast

Each one keys its own leaderboard — a lap in the GT3 only races other GT3s.

GT3 · Closed cockpit

Falcon GT3

Downforce and forgiveness. The one to learn the circuit in — planted, predictable, quick everywhere.

Open wheel

Vortex OW-1

The fast, nervous one. Featherweight, brutal grip, zero patience for a clumsy input. Pure lap time.

Sports · Road

Kaze RS

Less grip, more slip. Manual box, real weight transfer — the driver's car of the three.
